posts.title: Commodore 128 Keyboard support in 64 Mode via ROM patch
posts.description: Credit: Evan-Amos CC BY-SA 3.0 (unmodified) The Commodore 128 has an extra 26 keys, with 24 additional keys in the key matrix, and 2 additional keys hardwired inputs to 8502 (Caps Lock) and MMU (40/80 Display or ASCII/DIN). Unfortunately, these keys are not normally accessible when in Commodore 64 mode -- until now, via KERNAL patches. To try out, run the program " 64MODE PATCH " which copies the BASIC & KERNAL ROMs into RAM, applies patches in RAM, and switches operation to run the ROMs from RAM. It is expected that extra keys do not work before the patch, and do work after the patch. Only the numeric keypad and separate cursor keys work with this patch. Alternatively, the folder 64mode-ROM-patches/ contains two .txt files, one for patching BASIC ROM, and another for patching KERNAL ROM. For instance, if you are running VICE emulator, there are ROMs in the C128 directory for 64mode: three versions for KERNAL, one for BASIC. posts.title: The Return of TypeScript 64 Emulator
posts.description: I programmed this back in 2020. It's a port of my Commodore 64 emulator from C++ to TypeScript/Web. It supports both BASIC and 6502/6510 programs with D64 drive image (drag and drop, read-only). Live link: https://c64.davevw.com (recommend scaling window to see it bigger) But I didn't get the keyboard just right, it was registering keys on release only. And I didn't know what the fix was. Well, given six years have now passed, there are some assistants out there that are willing to give it a go for FREE! So thanks GitHub Copilot for working with me on a Saturday to investigate and solve the issue. Seems it had something to do with how when yielding from the Web Worker background service that is the heart of this emulator, while keystrokes and UI are in the scope of the web page with a canvas. With a few more additions, the following platforms are also supported for EPROM or emulator .bin file: 128 plus/4 or 16 (264 series) Vic-20 All of these, plus the 64 are now supported via c-keymaps on github . (Alternatively drivers are supported in the same project for 128 and Vic-20 for remapping in real-time, using additional system resources, which also allows remapping of the Alt keymap for 128) Figure 2.
